title: How Did Ancient Humans Keep Food Without a Fridge?
notes: Tone and rhythm follow the Max cro reference: second person, staccato lists of three, sentences split across cuts, the voiced objection, short pauses (reference median 0.13 s). Each line is spoken in one pass; each phrase is one shot.

phrases: Tonight, a machine in your kitchen will hum in the dark.
All of it, safe for days.
Now take time back fifty thousand years.
A hunter has just brought down an antelope.
And more meat than they can eat.
Under this sun, it will rot within days.
So he has to solve a problem
you have never once thought about.
Now your brain is probably saying,
Cavemen? They just let it rot.
At least, that's what we assume.
Trick one: the sun and the wind.
Hung up to dry, thin strips keep for weeks.
It dries the meat, and keeps the flies away.
He shares the meat with the whole camp.
Next week, someone else gets lucky,
